task.title: Student card
task.description: Declare a constant studentName with your name and a constant courseName with the value "JavaScript". Declare a variable lessonsDone with let and the value 0, then on a separate line assign it 1. Print the name, the course name and the number of finished lessons to the console. Do not use var.

tests.name: The constant studentName holds a non-empty string
tests.fail: Declare const studentName = "Your name"; - the name in quotes.

tests.name: studentName is declared with const
tests.fail: The name does not change during the program, so it needs const, not let.

tests.name: The constant courseName equals "JavaScript"
tests.fail: You need const courseName = "JavaScript"; - letter case matters.

tests.name: lessonsDone is declared with let and the value 0
tests.fail: Declare let lessonsDone = 0; - the value will change later, so let.

tests.name: After the change lessonsDone equals 1
tests.fail: On a separate line assign the new value: lessonsDone = 1; - without let.

tests.name: The console shows the name, the course and the number of lessons
tests.fail: Use console.log(...) for studentName, courseName and lessonsDone after the change.

tests.name: The program runs without errors
tests.fail: There is an error in the code. Read it: a TypeError on assignment means lessonsDone was declared with const.

hints: A string is written in quotes: const studentName = "Anna";
const - the value does not change, let - it changes. The course does not use var.
Changing a value is written without let: lessonsDone = 1;
Printing to the console: console.log("Student:", studentName);

questions.question: What is JavaScript responsible for on a page?
options: Behaviour: reacting to user actions and changing the page
Storing the website on a server
questions.explanation: HTML - structure, CSS - appearance, JavaScript - behaviour.

questions.question: How do you correctly connect the file js/main.js to a page?
questions.explanation: An external file is connected with <script> and the src attribute; defer runs the code after the HTML is parsed.

questions.question: What does the defer attribute do?
options: Runs the script after the browser has parsed the whole HTML
Runs the script before CSS loads
Hides the code from the user
questions.explanation: With defer the script downloads in parallel and runs when the document is already parsed.

questions.question: Which command prints a message to the console? Type the command name without parentheses.
questions.explanation: console.log("Hello"); - output to the DevTools console.

questions.question: Which declarations follow the course style?
questions.explanation: The course does not use var, and a name cannot start with a digit.

questions.question: What happens: const year = 2025; year = 2026;
options: TypeError: a constant cannot be assigned a new value
Nothing, the second line is skipped
questions.explanation: A constant cannot be changed after declaration. A changing value needs let.

questions.question: Match the code with its meaning.
pairs: Comment until the end of the line
Print the value to the console
questions.explanation: A declaration is written once with let or const, an assignment - without them.

questions.question: Which variable names are valid?
questions.explanation: A hyphen means minus, and let is a reserved word. The course uses camelCase: userName.

questions.question: Does JavaScript distinguish userName and username?
options: Yes, they are two different variables

questions.question: Which key opens DevTools in Chrome and Edge on Windows? Type the key name.
questions.explanation: F12 or Ctrl+Shift+J (Cmd+Option+J on Mac) opens the console.

questions.question: The console shows a red line: ReferenceError: scor is not defined. What does it mean?
options: A name is used that was not declared: most likely a typo in score
questions.explanation: ReferenceError - a reference to a name that does not exist. Compare the spelling with the declaration.

questions.question: Match the technology with the question it answers.
pairs: What happens when the user acts?
questions.explanation: The three technologies work together, each in its own file.
